key_insight: A Delphi-informed readmission model built from inpatient EMR data and clinical notes modestly predicted 30-day heart failure readmission, but performance remained limited.
clinical_relevance: This suggests hospitals may need better, more reliable inpatient data capture to support targeted discharge planning and transitional care for heart failure patients.
method: Retrospective prognostic study using Calgary EMR data from 2011–2019
Included 15,160 adult heart failure hospitalizations with at least 1 year of follow-up
Used modified Delphi-selected variables and NLP extraction from clinical notes to build competing-risk survival models
evidence_signal: The final model achieved a C-statistic of 64.4 for 30-day readmission prediction, with 90- and 365-day outcomes and death analyzed as competing risks.
watch_item: Several variables considered important were not collected reliably enough for modeling, which may limit real-world implementation and model improvement.
paper_title: Developing a Heart Failure Readmission Model From Inpatient Electronic Medical Record Data
